title: Unicode confusable identifier boundary for unresolved continuity artifacts
memory: Unicode confusable normalization may be used to discover candidate references, but a normalized or skeleton-equivalent token is not the canonical identifier and cannot establish immutable provenance without exact-source agreement.

observed: The canonical unresolved identifiers in ACTIVE_QUEUE.json are the exact ASCII strings M-004, M-005, and M-006.
Repository code search for the exact ASCII token M-004 returned no indexed candidates in this run.
Frontier Research R-029 defines a fail-closed construction boundary for a verified Unicode confusables dataset, but its production dataset integration remains incomplete.
inferred: Historical text may contain visually similar dash, letter, or digit code points that are not byte-identical to the canonical identifiers.
Confusable or normalization-aware discovery could expand recall, but automatic canonicalization would create false provenance and namespace-collision risk.
proposed: Search exact ASCII identifiers first, then explicitly enumerate Unicode dash and confusable variants as candidate-only queries.
Store every variant with original code points, source locator, normalization form, skeleton digest, namespace, owner, semantic role, and temporal position.
Promote a candidate to canonical provenance only when the immutable source itself assigns the exact canonical identifier or a retained decision object explicitly records the alias relationship.
Treat normalization, case folding, and confusable skeletons as retrieval aids rather than identity mutation operations.
superseded: A visually identical token is equivalent to the canonical identifier.
A confusable skeleton match alone resolves M-004, M-005, or M-006.
Normalization may overwrite the original source token in provenance records.
unresolved: No exhaustive Unicode-variant search has yet been performed across all accessible branches, reachable commit trees, decision logs, language lexicons, project documents, chat history, and File Library sources.
The canonical source objects assigning M-004, M-005, and M-006 remain unlocated.
R-029's verified confusables dataset has not yet been promoted for production use.

contradiction_resolution.apparent_conflict: A look-alike identifier may be relevant to provenance while not being the canonical identifier.
contradiction_resolution.resolution: Relevance and identity are separate claims. Confusable equivalence can justify candidate inspection, but only immutable exact-source or explicit alias evidence can establish canonical identity.

source_status.use: Defines exact unresolved ASCII identifiers and acceptance criteria.

source_status.source: GitHub exact-token code search for M-004
source_status.use: Returned no candidate in this run; does not prove historical absence.
Supplies the verified-confusables construction boundary and its remaining limitations.

falsification_route: Locate an immutable source whose original token is a Unicode-confusable variant and which explicitly declares that variant an alias of one canonical M identifier.
Show that promoting skeleton-equivalent tokens without exact-source agreement produces no collisions across all relevant namespaces.
Demonstrate that original code points can be discarded without changing provenance conclusions.
